violations.where: Data model → Credit Note: `credit_note_number` "own `CN-` sequence, strictly sequential; kept separate from `invoice_number`"; R-d11; S31
violations.why: The Sheet decision d:credit_note_numbering states credit notes "share the invoice number sequence." The spec does the exact opposite — a separate CN- sequence — silently reversing the decision it cites.
violations.fix_hint: Either update the Sheet decision to a separate sequence, or number credit notes within the invoice sequence as the Sheet dictates.

violations.where: Invoice lifecycle lists 7 states incl. `viewed`; Data model Invoice `status` enum = (draft,sent,partially_paid,paid,overdue,void) with no `viewed`
violations.why: The lifecycle section adds a `viewed` state and sent→viewed transition, but the Invoice status enum and status-derivation in the data model have no `viewed` state at all. The two sections disagree about the set of legal Invoice states.
violations.fix_hint: Reconcile: either add `viewed` to the enum/derivation or remove the `viewed` state from the lifecycle.

violations.where: Invoice lifecycle row `sent`→`viewed` | Who: Client | "Client receives and opens the invoice" vs permissions Client column all ✗ and note 2 "performs no in-app action" and non-goals "no email open-tracking or 'viewed' signal"
violations.why: The lifecycle has the Client (an actor with no account and no in-app action) drive a state transition, and relies on an open/viewed signal the permissions prose and non-goals both say does not exist. The scenario the lifecycle describes is forbidden by the permission matrix and explicitly denied elsewhere.
violations.fix_hint: Remove the Client-driven `viewed` transition; there is no viewed signal or Client action in v1.

violations.where: Invoice status derivation + R-r3 balance cap (amount − payments − credits) + R-r7 (paid iff payments==amount)
violations.why: With any credit note applied, R-r3 caps recordable payments at amount−credits, so payments can never equal amount, so R-r7's `paid` is unreachable. Meanwhile status derivation only defines sent (requires credited_amount==0), partially_paid (requires amount_paid>0), and paid (amount_paid==amount). A credited invoice with amount_paid=0 (e.g. $450 invoice, $200 credit) matches NO status and can never leave it — an unsatisfiable, statusless stuck record.
violations.fix_hint: Add an explicit 'settled/closed-by-credit' status and make status derivation exhaustive for any credited invoice.

violations.where: Permissions matrix "Review a Statement | Bookkeeper ✓" vs Statement lifecycle `generated`→`reviewed` | Who: Firm Owner only (⟨a8⟩)
violations.why: The matrix grants the Bookkeeper the ability to review a Statement, but the Statement lifecycle allows only the Firm Owner to perform the review transition. The two sections disagree about who can review; the Sheet action a8 is Firm-Owner-only.
violations.fix_hint: Deny Bookkeeper review in the matrix or add a Bookkeeper review transition — but a8 restricts review to the Firm Owner.

violations.where: R-r5 / permissions note 1 / Delegation entity — Bookkeeper with delegation may void
violations.why: Sheet r5 states "Only the Firm Owner may void an invoice." The spec weakens this by granting a delegated Bookkeeper void rights. The Sheet's own x7 conflicts with r5's "only," and the spec resolves toward x7, contradicting the literal inviolable rule.
violations.fix_hint: Reconcile r5 and x7 at the Sheet level before implementing delegated void.

violations.where: R-r6 / permissions note 1 — Bookkeeper with delegation may change monthly rate
violations.why: Sheet r6 states "Only the Firm Owner may change a client's monthly rate," but the spec permits a delegated Bookkeeper to do so, weakening the rule's "only."
violations.fix_hint: Reconcile r6 and x7 at the Sheet level before implementing delegated rate change.

violations.where: R-d2 "An Invoice's `amount` equals the sum of its Line Item `amount` values" vs Invoice derived `amount` = `subtotal` − `discount_amount`
violations.why: R-d2 asserts amount is the plain sum of line items, but the Invoice model subtracts a whole-invoice discount. When a discount exists the two definitions disagree.
violations.fix_hint: Restate R-d2 as amount = subtotal − discount_amount.

omissions.why: Permissions note 2 cites ⟨src: n:n11⟩ which does not exist in the Sheet noun list (n1–n6); dangling/incorrect trace marker.

Sheet decisions d:auto_reminder_schedule (two automatic nudges) and d:late_fee_basis (flat late fee) are contradicted by the spec's manual-only reminders and no-late-fee stance; they conflict with d:overdue_reminders/d:late_fees but the spec never explicitly resolves the contradiction.

scope_creep.item: system
User
Delegation
Credit Note
Firm Settings
The sum of Payment amounts applied to an Invoice may never exceed its outstanding balance (amount minus applied payments minus applied credit-note amounts); no overpaid or negative balance can arise.
A paid Invoice cannot be edited; corrections require voiding it and issuing a new Invoice.
No entity is ever hard-deleted; records leave active use only by void (Invoice) or archived (Client) status, including through bulk actions.
For every Line Item, amount = round-to-cents(quantity × rate); a computed amount of zero or negative is rejected.
An Invoice's amount equals the sum of its Line Item amounts minus any single whole-invoice discount, and must be greater than zero to send.

All monetary values are stored as positive integer cents in a single currency; reductions (payments, credit notes) are stored positive and subtracted, so a balance only decreases toward zero and never below it.
When a Client's billing_day does not exist in a given month, the invoice and due dates use the last day of that month.
A Send or Record-Payment action fired twice with the same idempotency key is detected and applied once; the duplicate is ignored.
When an Invoice is sent but the email fails, the Invoice remains sent and delivery_status is set to delivery_failed for retry; it is never silently dropped or held in draft.
Undo affects only the most recent field edit on a draft Invoice or a Client; it can never change an Invoice's status and can never touch a paid or void Invoice.
Credit notes are numbered in a separate CN- sequence so they never consume invoice numbers.
Each mutable record carries a version; a save whose submitted version differs from the stored version is rejected and the editor is shown the current record.
No Invoice, Line Item, or Statement carries a tax field, and all amounts are in one currency.
Every sent Invoice PDF is rendered from the firm's configured branding, set only by the Firm Owner.
Initial CSV import is available only while the firm has no Invoices; after first successful use it is disabled.
Archiving a Client sets status archived and keeps all its Invoices and Payments intact; there is no cascade delete and no restore path in v1.
The Client holds no account, has no session, and performs no in-app action; it only receives the Invoice PDF by email with no login, portal, or open-tracking.
Only the Firm Owner may invite or manage user accounts, set Service default rates, issue credit notes, grant delegations, and edit firm branding.
An invoice's due_date is issue_date + net_terms_days from Firm Settings.

Bookkeeper|export as CSV|Invoice

Bookkeeper|void (with delegation)|Invoice
Bookkeeper|undo last field edit on|Invoice
Bookkeeper|apply bulk action to|Invoice
Firm Owner|change monthly rate of|Client
Firm Owner|issue|Credit Note
Firm Owner|invite or manage|User
Firm Owner|grant|Delegation
Firm Owner|edit branding and invoice template of|Firm Settings
system|flag overdue|Invoice
No third-party integrations, public API, or webhooks; the accountant is served by file export only.
No multi-currency and no multi-organisation tenancy; one firm, one currency.
No automatic overdue reminders and no late fees; reminders are sent by hand.
No estimates, quotes, or time tracking that convert to invoices.
No deposits or up-front retainers applied to future invoices.
No hard deletion of any record, including through bulk actions.
No approval workflow; nothing is queued for a second party's sign-off.
No restore of an archived Client; archiving is one-way in v1.
No installed app and no offline mode; browser and online only.
